pr_title: Treat schedule time range as open ended, [FROM, to]
pr_body:
## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->
The old implementation treated the time interval as closed, meaning it included both endpoints FROM and TO.
However, the state gets updated only on these timestamps and therefore will never get back to OFF.
So, the 1st changed was to treat the time range as [FROM, TO).
However, this broke the special case of "24:00:00", so there is an additional fix for that as well.

pr_comments:
Hey there @home-assistant/core, mind taking a look at this pull request as it has been labeled with an integration (`schedule`) you are listed as a [code owner](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/CODEOWNERS#L947) for? Thanks!
<sub><sup>(message by CodeOwnersMention)</sup></sub>

@amitfin Can you please give some examples of how the behavior changes with your PR:
- A schedule with a single time range - This is what this PR is aiming to fix?
- A schedule with adjacent time ranges, which do not cross at midnight - There will now be glitch ON->OFF->ON between the events?
- A schedule with adjacent time ranges, which do cross at midnight - This is what a workaround has been added for?

@emontnemery, here are more details about the scenarios:
- A schedule with a single time range
  - Before this change, the state would NEVER change to STATE_OFF. This is a major bug in the implementation which has to be fixed, and this is the trigger for the change. The only times (with the exception of startup) the state gets updated are CONF_FROM and CONF_TO and in both cases the result was STATE_ON.
 - A schedule with adjacent time ranges, which do not cross at midnight
   - The state will get updated 3 times: (1) CONF_FROM1, (2) CONF_TO1 / CONF_FROM2, and (3) CONF_TO2. In the first 2 events it will be STATE_ON, and in the last STATE_OFF (the result of the last event is different from the original implementation, but it's not really related to adjusted time periods.)
- A schedule with adjacent time ranges, which do cross at midnight - This is what a workaround has been added for?
  - This PR is not about midnight (and the special case of "24:00:00"), but about the original bug where the state would never get set to STATE_OFF. However, when fixing that bug (which we have to fix), there was a regression in the midnight logic, so it got fixed as well. Just to be clear: the original midnight logic was correct for the old implementation (but the old implementation was wrong.) There is one difference between the old midnight logic and the new one: with the old logic there were 4 events (CONF_FROM1, CONF_TO1, CONF_FROM2, CONF_TO2). With the new logic there are only 3 events as we combine CONF_TO1 and CONF_FROM2 to a single event, which is the same as we do to adjusted time ranges which are not crossing at midnight.
 
Does it make sense?

Thanks @amitfin for explaining, it all makes sense 👍 
(And I should have noticed the bug when adding the test `test_events_one_day` just a few days ago 🤦)

I pushed a commit to make sure we test the behavior of adjacent events within the same day.
Could you help review the tests I added @amitfin ?
I reviewed the test cases. They look great. Thank you!

issue_context.title: Schedule has wrong time range calculation
issue_context.body:
### The problem

The current implementation treats the time interval as closed, meaning it includes both endpoints (FROM and TO).
However, the state gets updated only on these timestamps. So, for example, a schedule with a single time range will always stay ON.
This is demonstrated in the test case [test_events_one_day](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/a9fe9857bde9f878e91d39607a7223d90b4e3b61/tests/components/schedule/test_init.py#L224). As can be seen the state stays ON.
This can be fixed by changing the condition [here](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/a9fe9857bde9f878e91d39607a7223d90b4e3b61/homeassistant/components/schedule/__init__.py#L298). However, it breaks the behavior when TO is midnight (and the test cases test_adjacent and test_to_midnight).

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

2022.9

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

_No response_

comments:
Hey there @home-assistant/core, mind taking a look at this issue as it has been labeled with an integration (`schedule`) you are listed as a [code owner](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/CODEOWNERS#L947) for? Thanks!
<sub><sup>(message by CodeOwnersMention)</sup></sub>

A possible way to fix it is to use a special value (or "00:00:00") on the TO of the last time range of the day for marking the end of the day, instead of "24:00:00" which is currently being used (which gets translated to "23:59:59.999999".)
But this is a special case that needs to be handled in a few places in the code, so maybe there are more clever ways to do it.
Anyway, the test case "test_adjacent" is very important. Otherwise, some (physical) devices can get damaged by the off/on flickering (e.g. some old AC units are quite sensitive to that.)

The above PR solves both issues:
1) The time range is treated as open ended, so when the end event is fired the state changes to OFF.
2) There is a special treatment of midnight, so it behaves correctly when there is an adjusted time range.
Note that there is a change from the previous behavior in case there are 2 adjusted time ranges which meet at midnight. The previous implementation had 2 different events, one for time.max of the 1st day and another one for midnight of the 2nd day. With the new implementation there is only a single event at midnight of the 2nd day. IMHO, this is a better behavior as this is also the behavior when there are 2 adjusted time ranges which meet at any other time of the day (the midnight was the exception here in term of behavior, and now this exception was removed.)
